topic: Cristiano Ronaldo's journey in Saudi Arabia with Al-Nassr
summary: Ronaldo left Manchester United in November 2022 and joined Al-Nassr as a free agent on 30 December 2022. His contract has never been published, so all pay numbers are estimates. No source shows any Saudi law changed for him: lawyers said enforcement against foreigners had eased generally. He won his first Saudi league title in May 2026, married Georgina in Portugal in August 2026, is on about 985 goals, and his deal runs to June 2027 while PIF explores selling the club.

timeline.event: Al-Muammar later says the idea of signing Ronaldo was first proposed by Prince Khalid bin Fahd. Same summer Al-Hilal also negotiates.

key_facts.fact: Ronaldo gave a TV interview to Piers Morgan (TalkTV) in November 2022 saying he felt betrayed by Manchester United; his contract was then ended by mutual agreement in November 2022 and he was a free agent. The sources we read say only 'November', so the exact day is not established here.
Al-Nassr announced the signing on 30 December 2022. Ronaldo arrived as a free agent, so no transfer fee to United is reported. AP says he had been a free agent since United ended his deal.

Contract length of the original deal: reports split between 'two-and-a-half years, until June 2025' (TNT, National, Romano, CBS) and 'two years' (SportBible, National in a later piece). Two and a half years fits the announced end of 2025.

Unveiling: Tuesday 3 January 2023 at Mrsool Park, Riyadh. The National describes the event as sold out in a 25,000-capacity stadium. Ronaldo said: 'I'm so proud to make this big decision in my life, in football.'
key_facts.reported_by: The National, Gulf News, club video

key_facts.fact: At the unveiling Ronaldo said it was 'not the end of my career to come to South Africa', a slip for Saudi Arabia; reported wording varies slightly. South African Tourism replied on social media that it was 'patiently waiting'. The National's write-up prints the sentence as 'Saudi Arabia', so it silently corrected it.

WHO APPROACHED FIRST: the only first-hand account is from then-club president Musalli Al-Muammar, speaking to Al Arabiya in December 2025. He says the idea began in July 2022 after a proposal from Prince Khalid bin Fahd, a former 'golden member' of the club. This is one interested party's retelling, read via summaries, not a document. Neither Ronaldo nor Regufe has confirmed it on record in what we found.
key_facts.reported_by: Al-Muammar via Al Arabiya, relayed by Foot Africa/OneFootball and Yalla Shoot/YSScores

key_facts.fact: Al-Muammar's account of the route: attempts through then-agent Jorge Mendes; a trip to Manchester with Mohamed Al-Khuraiji that failed to produce a meeting; tension between Ronaldo and Erik ten Hag changed things; contact through a family member; a first direct meeting in Lisbon supervised by Sports Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Turki Al-Faisal; a second meeting in Qatar; Saad Al-Lazeez joined in the final hours. Quote relayed: Ronaldo 'wanted reassurance that it was a big project'.
Al-Muammar says Ronaldo signed TWO contracts, one with Al-Nassr and one with the Saudi Pro League. No contract has been published, so this is uncorroborated.

Mendes: AS and Marca (Dec 2022/Jan 2023) reported Mendes was not involved in the Al-Nassr deal and that Ricky Regufe, Ronaldo's personal manager and an ex-Nike executive, handled negotiations. This conflicts with Al-Muammar's 2025 account that the early attempts ran through Mendes. Both can be true (early route vs final deal) but no source settles it. Neither man has been quoted on record in what we found.
key_facts.reported_by: AS, Marca, Daily Mail via GiveMeSport; versus Al-Muammar

key_facts.fact: PIF: no source we found gives PIF a role in the original December 2022 approach. PIF only took control of Al-Nassr in June 2023. Al-Muammar names the Sports Minister, not PIF. Any claim that PIF signed Ronaldo is a guess.
key_facts.reported_by: Inference from Al-Muammar and SPA dates

key_facts.fact: Earlier Saudi interest: summer 2022 Al-Hilal. Search-result text says Ronaldo discussed a £305m offer on TalkTV, and we could not open a primary transcript. Press reports gave about EUR 242m over two years (The Athletic via Orange) and $228m, so the amount is disputed. Al-Hilal president Fahad bin Nafel said 'Yes, we negotiated with Ronaldo. The problem was not in the money'; GOAL ties the collapse to a FIFA transfer ban on Al-Hilal. Ronaldo says he refused because he was happy at United; the president's version differs.
key_facts.reported_by: Ronaldo on TalkTV; Al-Hilal president; The Athletic

key_facts.fact: PIF takeover: on 5 June 2023 the sports ministry and SPA announced PIF would own 75% of Al-Nassr, Al-Hilal, Al-Ittihad and Al-Ahli, with non-profit foundations holding 25%.

Ownership since: in August 2026 the Sports Ministry moved the remaining 25% of Al-Nassr to PIF, reportedly giving PIF 100%. In April 2026 PIF agreed to sell 70% of Al-Hilal to Kingdom Holding for $320m.
key_facts.reported_by: Enterprise AM; Saudi journalist Khaled Al-Rasheed via World Soccer Talk

key_facts.fact: NEITHER CONTRACT HAS BEEN PUBLISHED. Al-Nassr and Ronaldo have not disclosed the salary in either deal. Every money figure in this file is a press estimate unless stated otherwise.
key_facts.reported_by: Sky Sports, Yahoo/Reuters, Spoliamag noting undisclosed financials

key_facts.fact: Original deal, base: CBS Sports (James Benge, 23 Dec 2022, then with Ben Jacobs) reported about $75m a year in basic salary, with extra income from image rights it did not quantify. Bleacher Report and Fox repeated the $75m figure.
key_facts.reported_by: CBS Sports (Benge, Jacobs): single original report

key_facts.fact: Original deal, total: a source told AFP the deal was worth 'more than EUR 200m'. Reports including Romano's put the commercial-inclusive package near EUR 200m a year. GOAL's conversion is £177m ($215m) a year. The National: 'could be worth more than $200 million per year' including commercial tie-ins. The gap between $75m base and $200m+ total is image rights and commercial deals, split not published.

2030 ambassador money: Marca reported a contract clause making him a bid ambassador; media reported an extra EUR 200m for it. Al-Nassr denied it on 11 January 2023: 'Cristiano Ronaldo's contract with Al Nassr does not entail commitments to any World Cup bids.' We found a CLUB denial, not a personal denial by Ronaldo.

Extension timeline: AFP quoted a club official on 10 Feb 2025 about a one-year extension to June 2026, then the deal changed. Marca, 15 Jan 2025, reported EUR 183m a year (GOAL's conversion £154m/$188m) and a 5% stake offer in GOAL's retelling. Al-Nassr announced a two-year contract on 26 June 2025, until 2027.
key_facts.reported_by: Al-Nassr (fact of deal); AFP and Marca (earlier reports)

key_facts.fact: Extension money, SINGLE ORIGIN: The Sun, 26 June 2025, is the origin of the viral breakdown: £178m a year base (£488,000 a day), about £492m in total, £24.5m ($33.7m) signing bonus rising to £38m ($52.3m) if year 2 is triggered. GOAL, SI, SportBible, VnExpress and a-sports all relay the same story, so they are NOT independent confirmations. The £492m does not reconcile with its parts in GOAL's retelling (£178m x 2 = £356m).
key_facts.reported_by: The Sun (unnamed sources), relayed by GOAL, SI, SportBible

key_facts.fact: Extension extras (all The Sun-origin, none confirmed): Golden Boot bonus £4m ($5.5m); title bonus £8m ($11m); AFC Champions League bonus $8.94m; $110,000 a goal and $55,000 an assist, up 20% in year two; private jet allowance £4m ($5.5m in SI, $4.5m in VnExpress); 16 household staff (3 drivers, 4 housekeepers, 2 chefs, 3 gardeners, 4 security) at about £1.4m ($1.93m) a year; about £60m in projected Saudi commercial deals.
The title bonus: Al-Nassr won the 2025/26 title, so if the reported £8m bonus exists it would have paid out. No report confirms payment.
key_facts.reported_by: Our inference from The Sun's report and the title

key_facts.fact: Outlier: NBC Sports (1 July 2025) printed 'up to $468 million per year', '$936 million' in total, attributing it only to 'reports'. No other credible outlet carries this, and it is over twice The Sun's figure. Do not use.

Stake: The Sun's sources said 15% of the club, worth £33m (SI converts to about $45.4m). Daily Mail carried the same 15% (per VnExpress). GOAL in Jan 2025 said 5% was offered.  In Sept 2026 Asharq Business and A Bola reported something else: a contract clause giving him PRIORITY on 20% if the club opens to private investors. World Soccer Talk, citing Saudi journalist Khaled Al-Rasheed (Oct 2026), says PIF owns 100% and Ronaldo is not a confirmed shareholder. So a stake is unconfirmed and, as of the latest reports, not completed.
key_facts.reported_by: The Sun, Daily Mail, Marca/GOAL; Asharq Business, A Bola; Al-Rasheed

key_facts.fact: Status today: the contract runs to June 2027, per ESPN and UPI. He reportedly had a release clause of EUR 50m (£44m) active in summer 2026 (Record's CEO Pedro Sousa via World Soccer Talk, not confirmed) and he stayed.

Per-match fee: WE FOUND NO REPORT OF A FIXED APPEARANCE FEE. Reports only mention salary plus goal/assist bonuses. Any 'he earns $X a match' number is somebody dividing salary by games. Our own division is in pay_breakdown and is labelled as such.
key_facts.reported_by: Absence of reporting; The Sun only reports goal/assist bonuses

key_facts.fact: Forbes 2023: No.1, $136m, $46m on field, $90m off. 2024: No.1, $260m, $200m on field, $60m off. 2025: No.1, $275m, $225m on field, $50m off. 2026: No.1, $300m, $235m on field, $65m off (window 1 May 2025 to 1 May 2026, before tax and agent fees). These are Forbes ESTIMATES, not contract data. Our note: the 2023 figure's window ended about May 2023, so it covers only months of Saudi pay.
key_facts.reported_by: Forbes, via Wikipedia table; 2025 confirmed by The National; 2026 by Forbes byline and Visual Capitalist

key_facts.fact: Forbes (May 2026) also puts his net worth at $1.2bn and says he is the first active athlete past $2bn career earnings. That reading comes via search result text from a Forbes page that blocked direct reading.

Billionaire: on 8 October 2025 Bloomberg's Billionaires Index estimated him at about $1.4bn, the first footballer it classed as a billionaire, per Reuters. It said he earned over $550m in salary from 2002 to 2023. It is an estimate; Ronaldo has not published his wealth. Forbes' later $1.2bn is lower, so the range is $1.2bn to $1.4bn.

Tax: PwC says Saudi Arabia has no individual income tax on employment income. We found NO credible report on Ronaldo's own tax position, including on off-field income earned outside Saudi Arabia, so say 'Saudi Arabia does not tax salaries', not 'he pays no tax'. Forbes figures are pre-tax.

PREMISE UPDATE: Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez are no longer unmarried. They married in a civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, on 11 August 2026, attended by their five children, after an engagement announced 11 August 2025. The ceremony was not in Saudi Arabia. Any script must say 'lived together unmarried until August 2026'.
key_facts.reported_by: ESPN, Al Jazeera/AFP citing Ronaldo's representatives

key_facts.fact: What the law said: reports repeat that Saudi law forbids unmarried cohabitation, but no outlet we read names a statute or article. UK government travel advice (current page) states: 'Sex outside of marriage and adultery are illegal, including for tourists.' It does not specifically address cohabitation.
key_facts.reported_by: UK FCDO; Euronews on lack of statute

key_facts.fact: THE 2019 RULE PREDATES HIM BY OVER 3 YEARS: in October 2019, alongside the first tourist visa scheme, Saudi Arabia dropped the need for foreign men and women to prove a relationship to share a hotel room; Saudis must still show proof. It covers hotels and tourists, not residents' housing. The US State Department and UK FCDO still state the hotel rule.
key_facts.reported_by: Saudi Tourism commission (Twitter), Reuters, Al Jazeera, CNBC

key_facts.fact: THE ORIGIN OF THE LEGAL STORY: EFE, 4 January 2023, the day after the unveiling, quoted two anonymous Saudi civil-law lawyers. One: 'Although the kingdom's laws still prohibit cohabitation without a marriage contract, the authorities have recently begun to turn a blind eye and no longer prosecute anyone', adding these laws are 'used when there is a problem or a crime'. Other: authorities 'today do not interfere in this matter' for foreigners, 'but the law continues to prohibit cohabitation outside of marriage'. Both describe the general treatment of foreigners, not a Ronaldo exception.
key_facts.reported_by: EFE (anonymous lawyers); single source relayed widely

key_facts.fact: Same EFE report: freedoms allowed to foreigners do not apply to Saudi nationals. It listed Georgina's possible routes: a separate visa sponsored by Al-Nassr, or a one-year tourist visa allowing 90 consecutive days per stay. We do not know which she used.

NO LAW WAS CHANGED FOR HIM, as far as any source shows. We found no decree, regulation, statement or lawyer's claim of a change specific to Ronaldo. The Saudi Personal Status Law was issued 8 March 2022 and took effect 18 June 2022, before his arrival, and is a general code. We found no official Saudi statement either way on his living arrangement.
key_facts.reported_by: HRW for the 2022 law; absence of any contrary record across EFE, Euronews, Newsweek

key_facts.fact: THE VIRAL LEAP: Newsweek (January 2023) wrote that he 'appeared to have had laws ... changed' and quoted X/Twitter users such as 'He made them bend their laws' and 'they can change their laws that are based on religion when the person is important enough', citing only the EFE lawyer. Tabloids and aggregators made it 'special permission'; SportBible's June 2025 article uses that phrase only in its headline, with a body saying authorities 'are said to have turned a blind eye'. Bio Bio Chile framed it as 'more perks for Ronaldo'.

The 2023 Saudi Civil Transactions Law: HRW says the Personal Status Law was part of four frameworks announced by the Crown Prince in February 2021, along with Civil Transactions, Penal Code for Discretionary Sanctions and Evidence. So the codification programme was announced before Ronaldo's arrival. We could not confirm the Civil Transactions enactment date or how the codes treat zina.

Faith: we found no statement by Ronaldo about being Catholic in our reading, so call him 'non-Muslim' only with care: fact-checkers show no conversion to Islam. Claims he made a shahada before King Salman use altered images (PRNigeria) and no statement or record supports conversion (Lead Stories). Former Al-Nassr goalkeeper Waleed Abdullah reportedly said Ronaldo showed interest, single-source and unverified.

Sujood: in May 2023 he dropped into a prostration after his winning goal in a 3-2 win over Al-Shabab, widely filmed. Goal compared it to Salah's celebration. New Arab says it is unlikely to reflect his faith. That is an opinion. He has not explained it in what we read.

Founding Day, 22 February 2023: Ronaldo wore a white thobe and daqlah, drank Arabic coffee and danced the Ardah with a ceremonial sword at the club, then posted 'Happy Founding Day to Saudi Arabia'. Al-Nassr published video.
key_facts.reported_by: The National, Gulf News, Ronaldo's Instagram

key_facts.fact: 99 lashes: FALSE. In September 2023, before Al-Nassr's AFC match at Persepolis in Tehran, Ronaldo met painter Fatemeh Hamami, who paints with her feet, and embraced her. Fact-checkers trace the punishment story to Iranian sites (Rouydad24, Sharq Emroz per one fact-check). The Iranian embassy in Spain denied on 13 October 2023 'the issuance of any court ruling against any international athlete'. NOTE: the owner's brief says 'Tractor'; the match was Persepolis, and we found no Tractor link.
key_facts.reported_by: Iranian embassy in Spain; Factly, BOOM, Africa Check

key_facts.fact: Discipline shows he is not outside the rules: after a 3-2 win at Al-Shabab on 25 February 2024, video showed him cupping an ear and thrusting his hand near his pelvis as 'Messi' chants rang out. The Saudi federation's Ethics and Discipline Committee suspended him one match, fined him SAR 10,000 (about $2,666) and ordered SAR 20,000 to Al-Shabab; non-appealable. He said the gesture is common in Europe.
key_facts.reported_by: SAFF committee; AP, Al Jazeera, ESPN

key_facts.fact: Alcohol: illegal. UK advice: 'It is illegal to drink alcohol or be drunk in public.' A Riyadh store opened January 2024 for non-Muslim diplomats; AP (December 2025) reports access quietly widened to non-Muslim Premium Residency holders, never officially announced. Ambassador Prince Khalid bin Bandar said 2034 World Cup will have no alcohol 'at the moment'. Nothing we found links this to Ronaldo.

Religion: UK advice says 'It is illegal to practise any religion other than Islam' but 'the Saudi authorities accept private practice of other religions.' A US-based commission urged Saudi Arabia to codify that right. Mecca: reports say entry is restricted to Muslims; we found no Saudi legal text in our reading and no Ronaldo angle.

Sportswashing: Amnesty International (Dana Ahmed), 4 January 2023: 'Al-Nassr's signing of Cristiano Ronaldo fits into a wider pattern of sportswashing in Saudi Arabia', urging him to raise human rights rather than give uncritical praise. Amnesty cited 81 people executed on a single day in 2022. He had called it an 'amazing country' at the unveiling the day before.

Leadership: Ronaldo attended the White House dinner for Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on 18 November 2025, with Trump saying his son Barron is a fan. Reports say he was among the last seated before MBS. We found no report of a one-on-one meeting.
key_facts.reported_by: ESPN, Al Jazeera, Fox News, Euronews

key_facts.fact: BEACH CLAIM: UNVERIFIED. We searched English and Arabic for a Saudi beach closed or reserved a full day for his family, including Red Sea, Sindalah, AMAALA and Jeddah terms, and found no report, tabloid or otherwise. We could not find where the rumour started. No source lets us call it true or call it false.

Closest documented story: January 2023 reports, originating with Spain's Mundo Deportivo and repeated by DNA India, ARY and others, that a Riyadh amusement park closed about 2 hours for the family. Outlets disagree on the venue (Boulevard World vs Winter Wonderland). GOAL's report on the same outing makes no closure claim. No park or official confirmed. This may be the seed of 'closed a place for his family'. That link is our inference.

Possible conflation (our inference only): in July 2015 a public beach on the French Riviera WAS closed for the Saudi royal party, a documented story about Saudi royalty and a beach, unrelated to Ronaldo.

What is documented: in July 2024 he posted 'Close to heaven' from Ummahat Island, Red Sea, with family on a beach; around June 2024 (a week after the King's Cup final, per Grazia; another outlet says March 2024) the family stayed at the St Regis Red Sea Resort, he posted 'Recharging'. Reports call the island 'private', and none mention a closure. Football Benchmark notes his July 2024 Red Sea post got 16m+ likes.
key_facts.reported_by: Ronaldo's Instagram via Lokmarg and Grazia

key_facts.fact: Documented purchase: in December 2025 Ronaldo and Georgina bought two villas (3- and 2-bedroom) at Nujuma, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve, in the Ummahat Islands about 26 km offshore, reached by boat or seaplane. Ronaldo via Saudi Gazette: 'truly exceptional in every sense of the word.' CEO John Pagano welcomed them. So he bought private villas in a private resort; it was not a gift, as far as reported. The price, about £7m in total, is The Sun's.
key_facts.reported_by: Saudi Gazette (quotes), Gulf News, GOAL; The Sun (price, unconfirmed)

key_facts.fact: Georgina's 2023 bikini photos: GOAL, May 2023, said she 'might run into trouble'. No legal text was cited and we found no consequence. Her 2024 Red Sea swimwear posts happened at a resort that had hosted Red Sea Fashion Week.

Other rumours we looked for without finding credible support: airport or stadium named after him in Saudi Arabia (Saudi naming: none found; the home ground has its own sponsor naming); 'King gave him a palace or island' (none; he bought the Nujuma villas). See claim_checks.

Four Seasons, Kingdom Tower, Riyadh: reports in January 2023 had the family in the two-storey Kingdom Suite (floors 48 and 50; 17 rooms). GOAL via The Mirror says 17 suites for family and entourage, which is a different claim. Cost: Gulf News says $300,000 a month (no source); others say $250,000 a month (from about $8,000 a night); The Mirror via GOAL, a total bill of £250,000 (Arabic GOAL: EUR 280,000). The hotel does not publish the price and Gulf News does not say who paid; The Mirror says he settled the bill. The user's 'EUR 250k a month' is not what we found.
key_facts.reported_by: Daily Mail, The Mirror, Gulf News, Supercar Blondie

key_facts.fact: Next home: The Mirror (February 2023) said he left the hotel for a house in a compound. Location was not confirmed: reports said Al Muhammadiyah or Al Nakheel. Robb Report Malaysia (Nov 2025) says he later downsized to a villa in Al-Muhammadiyah. We found no report of Diplomatic Quarter, Ramal or Arabian Ranches, and those are unsupported.
key_facts.reported_by: The Mirror, New Arab, Robb Report

key_facts.fact: March 2025 'living in fear' story: NST (credited to agencies) relays Portuguese and Spanish media about threats, four new bodyguards and a move to a property with a bunker. Ronaldo and Georgina have not commented. Treat as tabloid.
key_facts.reported_by: Unnamed Portuguese and Spanish media via NST

key_facts.fact: Cars: the documented item is a sponsor gift. In December 2024 Al-Nassr's BMW partner Mohamed Yousuf Naghi Motors gave the squad BMW XM cars with personalised plates, reportedly worth EUR 155,000 each. Georgina's Rolls-Royce to him was a Christmas 2022 gift before he moved. Bentley, Bugatti or other Saudi car 'deals' are unsupported; a report of Bugatti gifts cites one anonymous source. The claim he gave teammates Rolls-Royces after the title is false (Dubawa).
Staff: the only figure is The Sun's 16 staff, club-funded at about £1.4m. Unconfirmed.
Schools: no credible source names his children's school. Do not state one.
key_facts.reported_by: Absence of reports; New Arab mentions Al Nakheel for its schools only

key_facts.fact: Cristiano Jr: joined Al-Nassr's academy in January 2023 (reports said U13). Reports also place him at Mahd Academy, and he has trained with Real Madrid in 2026 per Gulf News. Age and team claims vary. He is a minor; treat carefully.

March 2026 regional crisis: The Sun, Daily Mail and GOAL said his private jet flew Riyadh to Madrid after a drone strike on the US Embassy in Riyadh and implied he left. PA and Al Riyadiyah said he was still in Saudi Arabia; the club posted photos; Romano called it fake. Thairath reported the family left. The jet's flight is confirmed; his being aboard is not.
key_facts.reported_by: PA, Al Riyadiyah, Romano vs The Sun, Daily Mail

key_facts.fact: Debut: 22 January 2023, as captain, 1-0 win over Al-Ettifaq. First goal: 3 February 2023, stoppage-time penalty, 2-2 at Al-Fateh. First hat-trick and more: all four goals, 4-0 over Al-Wehda, 9 February 2023. Another first-half hat-trick at Damac, 25 February 2023.
key_facts.reported_by: TNT, Gulf News, The National, Wikipedia

key_facts.fact: 2022/23: no trophy; 19 apps, 14 goals all competitions (16 league, 14 league goals). Coach Rudi Garcia left in April 2023; Dinko Jelicic was interim.

Arab Club Champions Cup, 12 August 2023: Ronaldo scored both goals in a 2-1 extra-time final win over Al-Hilal, six in the competition. ESPN calls it 'unofficial'. Until May 2026 it was his only final win at Al-Nassr.
2023/24: 35 league goals, the Saudi Pro League single-season record, set 27 May 2024 in 4-2 win over Al-Ittihad, beating Hamdallah's 34 (2018/19). 51 apps, 50 goals in all competitions. Golden Boot.
Asia 2023/24: lost the AFC Champions League quarter-final to Al-Ain on penalties (4-4 aggregate, 3-1 shootout), 11 March 2024; he was the only Al-Nassr player to convert in the shootout.

Red card: 8 April 2024, Saudi Super Cup semi-final v Al-Hilal in Abu Dhabi, sent off in stoppage time for striking Ali Al-Bulayhi with his arm; 2-1 defeat. Reports said a two-match ban and SAR 20,000 fine were coming; we did not read the final ruling. NOTE: reported as a semi-final, not a final.
key_facts.reported_by: AP, Al Arabiya, Inside World Football

key_facts.fact: King's Cup final, 31 May 2024, Jeddah: 1-1, lost 5-4 on penalties to Al-Hilal. Ronaldo scored his penalty, then sank to the turf and sat in the dugout in tears as staff tried to comfort him. Mother-in-stands detail is unverified.

900th career goal: 5 September 2024, for Portugal v Croatia in Lisbon, in a 2-1 Nations League win, not for Al-Nassr. 2024/25: 41 apps, 35 goals; 25 league goals and Golden Boot again; third place in league.

Coaches at Al-Nassr since his arrival: Rudi Garcia (out April 2023), Dinko Jelicic interim, Luis Castro (July 2023 to 17 Sept 2024), Stefano Pioli (Sept 2024 to 25 June 2025), Jorge Jesus (July 2025 to May 2026, left after the title), Ange Postecoglou (current). Pioli left the day before Ronaldo's extension was announced.

PREMISE CORRECTION: the 'this chapter is over' post was on 26 May 2025 after a 3-2 loss at Al-Fateh, and the extension was announced 26 June 2025, one month later, not ten days. On 9 June he posted 'Future? Nothing will change.' 2024/25: lost AFC Champions League Elite semi to Kawasaki.

Club World Cup 2025: Al-Nassr did not qualify. Infantino said Ronaldo could join a participant. Ronaldo said he turned down offers. Sky's Solhekol says out of loyalty; another report ties it to recovery.

The February 2026 strike was real in reporting but is sourced: ESPN sources (2 Feb 2026) said he sat out a 1-0 win over Al-Riyadh in protest at PIF's lack of transfer activity versus other PIF clubs, after Benzema moved to Al-Hilal. He also missed Al-Ittihad (6 Feb). Ronaldo has not commented publicly in what we read. Games missed vary by source: two named games; Fox's URL says three.

League's response, to BBC Sport: 'no individual - however significant - determines decisions beyond their own club.' No named sanction found. Reported end: PIF settled salaries and funded the club, restoring Jose Semedo's authority (Now/Flashscore; thin source). He returned and scored on 14 February 2026 at Al-Fateh, per Wikipedia.
key_facts.reported_by: SPL via BBC (statement); NOW via Flashscore (resolution)

key_facts.fact: PREMISE CORRECTION: Al-Nassr WON the title. On 21 May 2026 they beat Damac 4-1 and Ronaldo scored twice, a free kick and a close-range finish, to win the 2025/26 Saudi Pro League, two points ahead of Al-Hilal. It is the club's first league title since 2018/19 and Ronaldo's first league title in five years. He broke down in tears, per reports.

Days before, on 16 May 2026, Al-Nassr lost the AFC Champions League Two final 1-0 at home to Gamba Osaka. ESPN counted four finals lost at Al-Nassr. Ronaldo's 2025/26: 37 apps, 30 goals (28 league). One relayed report says third in the Golden Boot race.
Saudi Super Cup final at the start of 2025/26: lost to Al-Ahli on penalties, per Nogomania (single low-tier source).

2026 World Cup: Portugal lost 1-0 to Spain in the round of 16. Ronaldo started all five matches and scored 3 (two in group, one penalty v Croatia), and said it was his last World Cup. Jorge Jesus became Portugal coach and says he would still pick him.
August 2026 Vogue interview (published 16 Aug): this is 'probably' his last year as a player. Not a formal retirement announcement.
key_facts.reported_by: Vogue via AFP/The Sun Malaysia, Bleacher Report

key_facts.fact: Oct 2026 Portugal rift: he left the Portugal squad during an international window after a dispute with Jesus over Nations League minutes, apologised, and the Portuguese FA suspended him around 10 Oct 2026. No final punishment published; investigation confidential.

Latest (as far as we could read, 2 Nov 2026): 2026/27, 12 apps, 9 goals for Al-Nassr to 30 Oct. Al-Nassr third on 28 points from 11 games (GOAL, Terrikon; Gulf News said second). He scored a hat-trick in a 5-3 win over Al-Kholood on 29 Oct. Coach Postecoglou rested him for 2 Nov at Pakhtakor; we found no report of that result. Next: Al-Hazem, 6 Nov.
key_facts.reported_by: Yahoo, Gulf News, GOAL table, Zamin citing Arriyadiyah, RonaldoStats

key_facts.fact: 1,000 goals: NOT reached. 985 career goals as of 30 Oct 2026, 138 for Al-Nassr in 160 matches. The tally includes a disputed 982nd (23 Oct, v Al-Faisaly): Opta rules it an own goal by Girotto, the league credits Ronaldo. Say 'about 985'. Security delay: on 12 Oct a Riyadh match waited an hour after a civil defence alert over Houthi missiles, then he scored goal 981.

2034 World Cup: at TOURISE in Riyadh, November 2025, he said he considers himself Saudi and wanted to help the 2034 bid. We found no formal ambassador title for 2034. He is the face of Saudi Tourism's 'Unreal Calendar' campaign.
key_facts.reported_by: Arab News, Saudi Gazette, Leaders MENA

key_facts.fact: Recruitment: 2023 window followed him with Benzema, Kante, Fabinho (Al-Ittihad), Neymar EUR 90m (Al-Hilal), Mane, Laporte (Al-Nassr). Causation by Ronaldo is argued, not proven. Joao Felix joined later; fee not sourced here. Jesus (July 2025): 'without Ronaldo I would not be here'.

Sale talks: Cardinale of RedBird told Gazzetta (Oct 2026) that interest in Al-Nassr is 'at a preliminary stage'. A Bola reports a five-member consortium including Ronaldo each committing at least $100m, about $500m in total; Sportitalia calls it preliminary and indirect. Club debt above SAR 800m (about $213m at the 3.75 peg) reportedly pushed a sale, and it faced a league transfer freeze. No deal announced.
key_facts.reported_by: Cardinale via UPI; A Bola, Asharq Business, Sportitalia via Enterprise

key_facts.fact: Followers: Gulf News, 10 January 2023: Al-Nassr Instagram up 1,072% to about 11m, implying roughly 1m before. Football Benchmark (March 2025): all-platform following up from under 5.2m to over 57.5m. Later: about 30m on Instagram per World Soccer Talk (unattributed). The owner's 0.8m figure is close but not sourced.
Spend: Deloitte says Saudi clubs spent a record $957m in summer 2023, second only to the Premier League, net $907m. By contrast, Enterprise AM says about $57m in summer 2026.

League revenue: SPL CEO Carlo Nohra is quoted as saying revenue rose 650%, mainly from broadcasts and commercial deals. World Soccer Talk says broadcasts grew from three territories to 140+, sources unnamed. A peer-reviewed study in Contemporary Economic Policy (Schreyer et al) found Ronaldo alone raised attendance demand; we read the abstract via search only.
Shirt sales: no credible figure found. Tourism gain attributable to him: no measurement found.

What he received beyond salary, documented: BMW sponsor car; Globe Soccer Best Middle East Player, Dubai, December 2025, third straight per Khaleej Times; a role fronting Saudi Tourism's campaign. Saudi 'residency' for him: no report. Streaming: from Sept 2026 a league 'Share and Earn' scheme could pay him, per ESPN, no amounts.
key_facts.reported_by: Khaleej Times, GOAL, Arab News, ESPN

case_status.justification: The story is established but its most-shared claims are not. Contract terms are unpublished; the 'law changed' and 'beach' stories have no primary support; Amnesty calls the signing sportswashing while Ronaldo publicly calls himself Saudi; and he remains in an active relationship with PIF, reported rift in February 2026 and sale talks.

closing_facts.last_update: 30 Oct-2 Nov 2026: 985 career goals, rested for Pakhtakor, third in league
closing_facts.latest_development: Cardinale confirmed preliminary interest in Al-Nassr (30 Oct 2026); Ronaldo said in August this is 'probably' his last year; suspended by Portugal pending outcome (Oct 2026); married 11 Aug 2026.
closing_facts.current_whereabouts: Riyadh; Al-Nassr captain, contract to June 2027. Home address unknown; villa in Al-Muhammadiyah per Robb Report.
closing_facts.recent_developments: First league title May 2026; World Cup exit July 2026; marriage; Portugal suspension; ownership moved to PIF 100% reportedly; RedBird consortium talks.

claim_checks.claim: Saudi Arabia changed its law for Ronaldo
claim_checks.evidence: No decree, regulation or official statement found. The 2019 hotel rule is three years earlier and general. Lawyers said the ban stays and enforcement against foreigners had eased generally. Sex outside marriage remains illegal per UK advice.
claim_checks.origin: EFE 4 Jan 2023 (anonymous lawyers: 'blind eye') amplified by Newsweek ('appeared to have had laws changed', quoting X users) and 'special permission' headlines.

claim_checks.claim: Saudi authorities gave Ronaldo 'special permission' to live with Georgina
claim_checks.evidence: Only anonymous lawyers saying enforcement is relaxed for foreigners generally. No Saudi official quoted, no permit reported.
claim_checks.origin: Tabloid headlines from Jan 2023, Telegrafi and SportBible.

claim_checks.claim: Ronaldo and Georgina still live together unmarried in Saudi Arabia
claim_checks.evidence: Married 11 Aug 2026 in Cascais, Portugal. True until that date.

claim_checks.claim: A Saudi beach was closed or reserved for a full day for his family
claim_checks.evidence: No report found in English or Arabic. Nearest: Riyadh amusement park 2-hour closure (Mundo Deportivo, unconfirmed), private Nujuma villas and Ummahat holidays. Could not be disproved.
claim_checks.origin: Not traced. Possibly a blend of the park report and the 2015 French Riviera beach closure for Saudi royals (our inference).

claim_checks.claim: A Riyadh amusement park closed 2 hours for the family
claim_checks.evidence: Mundo Deportivo, Jan 2023, repeated; venue names conflict; GOAL's report of the outing has no closure.

claim_checks.claim: He gets a fixed per-match fee
claim_checks.evidence: No outlet reports an appearance fee. All such figures are divisions of an estimated salary. The Sun reports goal and assist bonuses only. Contract unpublished, so it cannot be ruled out.
claim_checks.origin: Social posts dividing salary by games (no single origin traced).

claim_checks.claim: His salary is $200m a year (or EUR 200m)
claim_checks.evidence: Reported total package, not salary. CBS base about $75m in 2022. AFP source 'more than EUR 200m'. Forbes on-field $200m (2024) to $235m (2026). Nothing published.
claim_checks.origin: Dec 2022 CBS, Romano and AFP source.

claim_checks.claim: He earns $468m a year / $936m contract
claim_checks.evidence: NBC Sports only, attributed to 'reports'; conflicts with The Sun and Forbes.

claim_checks.claim: He was given a 15% stake in Al-Nassr
claim_checks.evidence: The Sun's sources and Daily Mail only (June 2025); earlier 5% (GOAL Jan 2025); later reports of a 20% priority clause (Asharq Business). Saudi journalist via WST says PIF 100%, Ronaldo not a confirmed shareholder.

claim_checks.claim: He is a paid ambassador for Saudi Arabia's 2030 World Cup bid
claim_checks.evidence: Al-Nassr: contract 'does not entail commitments to any World Cup bids'. Portugal itself co-hosts 2030. He later voiced support for 2034; no ambassador title found. Club denial, personal denial not found.
claim_checks.origin: Marca, Jan 2023; AFP source on EUR 200m extra.

claim_checks.claim: Iran sentenced him to 99 lashes
claim_checks.evidence: Iranian embassy in Spain denied any court ruling; fact-checkers agree; Hamami denied filing a complaint.
claim_checks.origin: Iranian sites, as reported by fact-checkers, Oct 2023; note this was the Persepolis trip, no Tractor link.

claim_checks.claim: He is the first billionaire footballer
claim_checks.evidence: Bloomberg index, about $1.4bn (Oct 2025), estimate. Forbes $1.2bn (2026). No audit.

claim_checks.claim: He converted to Islam / made shahada before King Salman
claim_checks.evidence: Altered images per PRNigeria; Lead Stories found no statement or record. A single second-hand comment from Waleed Abdullah is unverified.

claim_checks.claim: He did sujood on the pitch
claim_checks.evidence: Filmed May 2023. Meaning unexplained by him.

claim_checks.claim: The Four Seasons cost EUR 250k a month
claim_checks.evidence: Reports: $250k or $300k a month, or a £250k bill. Euro figure unsourced except Arabic GOAL's EUR 280k bill. No hotel confirmation.

claim_checks.claim: Saudi Arabia/King gave him a palace, island or stadium named for him
claim_checks.evidence: Nothing credible found; he bought Nujuma villas himself, per Saudi Gazette quotes; no Saudi stadium naming found. Sporting CP's gate 7 proposal is Portuguese.

claim_checks.claim: Al-Nassr gave him Bugatti/Rolls-Royce; he gave teammates Rolls-Royces
claim_checks.evidence: Teammate Rolls-Royce story is rated false (Dubawa). Club-side car documented is the BMW XM via sponsor. Bugatti gift rumour is anonymous, unverified.

claim_checks.claim: He fled Saudi Arabia on his jet in March 2026
claim_checks.evidence: Flight confirmed; PA, Al Riyadiyah and club photos say he remained; Thairath says family left.

claim_checks.claim: The extension came ten days after 'this chapter is over'
claim_checks.evidence: 26 May 2025 to 26 June 2025, one month.

claim_checks.claim: Arab Club Cup is still his only Al-Nassr trophy
claim_checks.evidence: 2025/26 Saudi Pro League won, 21 May 2026.

A tweet in Newsweek: 'He made them bend their laws instead of just marrying her.' He did marry her, three and a half years later, in Portugal.
Saudi Arabia did suspend him: one match, SAR 10,000, for a gesture aimed at fans chanting 'Messi', non-appealable.

He sat in the dugout crying after the King's Cup final.
He said 'this chapter is over'. A month later he signed for two more years.
In February 2026 he reportedly went on strike against the state fund that owns his club, and the league answered him without naming him: 'no individual - however significant...'.
Five days after losing an Asian final at home, he scored two to win the league at 41.
A Riyadh match was held for an hour after a missile alert in October 2026, then he scored.
He owns villas on a Red Sea island reached only by boat or seaplane.
